free_text: The patient is a 74-year-old male with an elevated PSA of 8.0 ng/mL and a clinical T1c prostate cancer. MRI shows a focal lesion in the transition zone with restricted diffusion, and pathology confirms Gleason 3+3 (ISUP Grade Group 1). The competing illness is Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia. Management assessment is active surveillance, balancing the potential benefit of treatment against patient preferences and the low-grade nature of the cancer.
